findings.claim: Question tariffs: 'Outline' at 3 marks, 'Explain' at 6 marks, 'Discuss' at 9 marks, 'Justify a Recommendation' at 12 marks.
findings.truth: Edexcel 1BS0 command words carry fixed tariffs: Outline 2, Explain 3, Discuss 6 (no context), Analyse 6 (context given by the question), Justify 9 (recommend one of two options), Evaluate 12. None of the four pairings above exists on the paper.
findings.evidence: spec Appendix 1 command word taxonomy; Paper 1 assessment overview (90 marks, Sections A 35 / B 30 / C 25)

findings.claim: 'On a 3-mark Outline question...' and 'On a 6-mark Explain question, only your best two points will be credited. Write two developed points...'
findings.truth: Outline is 2 marks. Explain is 3 marks and asks for one point with two expansions, not two developed points.

findings.claim: 'around 20% of UK start-ups do not survive their first year'
findings.truth: ONS Business Demography publishes a five-year survival rate of 39.4% for 2018 births but the bulletin page does not state a one-year rate; recent UK one-year survival has generally run near 90%, so the true first-year failure rate may be closer to 10%. Options: (a) leave the hedged 'around 20%' as a textbook figure, (b) replace with the sourced five-year figure ('about 6 in 10 do not survive five years'), (c) verify the one-year rate in the ONS dataset first.
findings.evidence: ONS Business demography, UK: 2023 bulletin (five-year survival 39.4%); one-year rate not published on that page
findings.ruling: NOTE: hedged 'around 20% fail in year one' left; ONS publishes five-year survival only.

findings.claim: 'Explain' at 6 marks (x2) and 'Analyse in Context' at 9 marks.
findings.truth: Explain is 3 marks. Analyse is 6 marks. There is no Edexcel question type called Analyse in Context.

findings.claim: 'On a 9-mark Analyse in Context...'
findings.truth: Analyse is a 6-mark question and the context is supplied by the question.

findings.claim: Outline at 3, Explain at 6 (x2), Discuss at 9, Justify a Recommendation at 12.

findings.truth: Spec 1.2.3 lists five: location, demographics, lifestyle, income and age. Age was missing from the Key Fact.

findings.claim: Q6 states a break-even point of 500 units with fixed costs 3,000, price 15 and variable cost 5, then concludes that after the variable cost rises to 7 the margin of safety 'increased' from 150 to 275 units.
findings.truth: With those figures the contribution is 10 and break-even is 300 units, not 500. After the rise the contribution is 8 and break-even is 375, so the margin of safety FALLS from 650-300 = 350 to 650-375 = 275. A rise in variable cost per unit can never raise the margin of safety, and the mark scheme reversed the direction the lesson itself teaches (n19, KC5, flashcards).
findings.evidence: recomputation from spec Appendix 3 break-even and margin of safety formulae

findings.claim: Q4 is labelled 'Analyse' with no context and its scheme says 'No context required for Analyse questions at this question type'; Q5 is 'Analyse in Context' at 9 marks.
findings.truth: Edexcel Analyse questions are always placed in context by the question; the no-context 6-mark question is Discuss. Analyse is 6 marks, not 9. All other break-even figures in the lesson recompute correctly (600 jars, 300 MoS, 400 units, 300 units, 100 mugs, 720/180 and 600/300 for Copperkettle).

findings.truth: Explain is 3 marks; the 6-mark contextual question is Analyse; Justify is 9 marks. Neither Analyse in Context nor Justify a Recommendation is an Edexcel question type, and the examiner claim is invented.

findings.claim: 'Four main factors shape where a business sets up: proximity to the market, proximity to labour, proximity to materials, and the impact of the internet.'
findings.truth: Spec 1.4.2 lists proximity to market, labour, materials AND competitors, with the nature of the business activity and the impact of the internet as separate factors. Proximity to competitors was dropped, and the lesson's own Key Fact contradicts the sentence by listing competitors as the fourth factor.

findings.truth: Outline 2, Analyse 6. The examiner claim is invented.

findings.claim: 'business objectives' is defined (in the dfn tooltip and the glossary) as 'The overarching goals of a business, such as survival, profit, growth or social impact, against which progress is measured.'
findings.truth: That is the definition of an AIM. Spec 1.3.1 and L6 of this unit both define an objective as a specific, measurable target set to work towards an aim. The lesson's own sentence around the tooltip says 'specific, measurable targets', so the tooltip reverses the aim/objective distinction the exam tests.

findings.claim: KC4: 'Employment law requires businesses to pay workers at least the National _____ Wage', keyed to 'Minimum' with 'Living' offered as a distractor.
findings.truth: For workers aged 21 and over the statutory floor is the National Living Wage, so the distractor is also a legal minimum. The keyed answer is still the standard GCSE term and the lesson names both, so the question is answerable. Recorded, not edited.
findings.evidence: spec 1.5.3 (principles of employment law: pay); the lesson's own text names both rates

findings.claim: Unit-wide: every banded mark scheme uses the band names Mastering / Secure / Developing / Emerging.
findings.truth: These are house names, not board wording, so they are not a copyright problem and are not on the validator's banned list. They do differ from the retro-fact-check house vocabulary (Top band / Upper-mid band / Mid band / Lower-mid band / Low band). Options: (a) leave them, since they are consistent across all 90 questions in the unit and across sibling units, or (b) run a separate fleet-wide rename. Recommendation: leave them and settle the vocabulary fleet-wide rather than in one unit.
findings.evidence: CHECK_PROMPT_GENERIC.md banned-string list and house vocabulary
findings.ruling: NOTE: band names left for the programme-wide band-ladder sweep.

findings.claim: Unit-wide: six questions keep the label '12 marks - Evaluate a Statement'.
findings.truth: The tariff is correct (Evaluate is 12 marks) and all six are genuine statement-evaluation questions, so the label is descriptive rather than a false board claim. The sibling invented labels (Analyse in Context, Justify a Recommendation) were removed because they carried impossible tariffs. Options: (a) leave, or (b) shorten to '12 marks - Evaluate' for consistency. Recommendation: shorten it in a fleet-wide pass, not here.
findings.ruling: NOTE: type label wording left for the question-type relabel sweep.

findings.claim: After the relabel, L1, L3, L9 and L14 each carry two 9-mark Justify questions, and the unit has only three 3-mark Explain questions across 15 lessons.
findings.truth: Not an error - every question is now a valid Edexcel command word and tariff - but the ladder is uneven. Adding one 3-mark Explain per lesson would need new questions authored, which is outside a fact-check pass.

summary: Every lesson carries impossible Edexcel 1BS0 command-word/tariff pairings (Outline at 3, Explain at 6, Discuss at 9, Analyse at 9, Justify at 12) in the practice questions and exam tips; 44 questions and 15 exam tips were relabelled to real tariffs with mark schemes retotalled. Four substantive content errors were also found and fixed: L7 Q6 states an impossible break-even (500 units where the data give 300) and concludes that a rise in variable cost RAISES the margin of safety when it falls from 350 to 275; L11 names the internet instead of proximity to competitors as one of the four spec location factors; L12 defines a business objective as an aim; L4 and L9 Key Facts undercount the spec lists (four segmentation bases for five, five long-term finance sources for six). Every calculation in L6, L7, L8, L9 and L15 was recomputed and, apart from L7 Q6, all are correct; all 75 knowledge-check answer keys are correct.
